title: The Monday Media Diet with Yu Su
summary: On Foundry, Granta, and Panda Delivery
content:
Today’s issue of WITI is brought to you by Cram, a colorful travel brand that’s making the business of packing a little more fun. Shop their gift sets here.

Yu Su is a DJ and producer. Check out her music here. -Colin (CJN)

Tell us about yourself.

I make music and play records or music files in many dark rooms of all sizes. And I live in North London.

My music is very much “in between.” Despite the genres, I’d say everything sits within this feeling of being under a deep ocean. You can hear what I mean on Foundry.

Describe your media diet.

Substack is a very new media diet that I’m in love with. Otherwise, I’m a regular reader of the Financial Times, New York Magazine, and The World of Interiors.

What’s the last great book you read?

The last book that I’ve almost finished is Ian Penman’s Erik Satie: Three Piece Suite.

Satie was a bowler hat and three-piece suit guy. Same outfit every day. A conceptual artist before there was a word for it. And Penman writes him as small, odd, unresolved. Not a monument. A breeze through the leaves. All of it a bit melancholy, a bit funny.

What are you reading now?

I haven’t started anything major. These last few days, I’ve just been reading the recent “American” issue of Granta. I’ve been reading it for a long time. Alongside FT Weekend, it’s essential reading for me to not go insane during those hours sitting in airports every weekend.

What’s your reading strategy when you pick up a print copy of your favorite publication?

It really depends. One funny strategy, or really just a bad habit, is that I only take the Life & Arts, Collecting, and magazine sections of FT Weekend. I barely read the rest, and they add a lot of volume to my bag.

Who should everyone be reading that they’re not?

The “everyone” bit in this question makes it very tricky to answer, so I’ll just assume it means the people I feel I relate to.

I would suggest New Juche, a Scottish writer. His words have hypnotic rhythms. It’s messy, where landscape and the sexual body merge, and senses carry heavy meaning.

In Mountainhead especially, the self-examination of all the contradictory feelings, thoughts, and impulses that shape his subjectivity is so present that sometimes I find it hard to get out of it.

I think he also never gets to exactly what he’s chasing, which I relate to deeply, if I’m honest.

What is the best non-famous app you love on your phone?

Well, this is probably a bit boring. I use a Chinese app called Panda Delivery to order produce and cooking ingredients. They have a very well-stocked Chinese supermarket online, where sometimes rare snacks show up.

Plane or train?

I rely on both.

What is one place everyone should visit?

Ghent in Belgium. I’ve said it many times, and I still stand by this statement: Ghent is spiritually similar to Kyoto.

Tell us the story of a rabbit hole you fell deep into.

Different profiles of vermouth? I drink vermouth and soda very often (since becoming a regular at The Plimsoll, happy birthday, guys!) and have decided to try to understand the different flavors of vermouth.

It’s just delicious.
